text:
Mira Chen: Heads up — after the onprem role refactor a customer hit a failure: their on-prem admin process cannot rotate KMS keys. It looks like RBAC precedence is causing an allowlist/service-owner binding to shadow the admin binding. Filing here before we escalate. @Jon any quick ideas? :exclamation:

Alex Gomez: Can you paste the principal + binding you're seeing? a short kubectl output is fine.

Mira Chen: Here are the relevant bits from their control plane (sanitized):
```
# kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o wide
NAME                          ROLE                             SUBJECT
onprem-service-owner-binding   clusterrole/service-owner        ServiceAccount:tenant:svc-edge
onprem-admin-binding          clusterrole/onprem-admin        User:mira-admin@example.com
```
When the rotation runs it fails with: `permission denied: kms.keys.encrypt` even though onprem-admin should have KMS privileges.

Samira: I pulled their control-plane audit logs — policy engine shows the evaluate order is: allowlist bindings -> tenant bindings -> explicit admin. The log shows: `deny: matched allowlist/service-owner precedence=100 override=true` — basically the service-owner allowlist is short-circuiting. Snippet: 
```
2026-03-19T14:22:11Z policy-eval INFO user=svc-edge result=DENY reason=allowlist/service-owner precedence=100 matched_rule=allow-tenant-ops
```

Jon Patel: Ugh. That ordering change was part of the refactor to short-circuit tenant allowlists for faster evals. We didn't consider KMS key-specific grants where admin principals must override. Two options: rollback the ordering change or add an explicit precedence exception for `onprem-admin`-scoped grants. I'd prefer a targeted fix (precedence exceptions) and a canary rollback if we see regressions.

security-bot: policy-change detected: `rbac-refactor-v3` deployed by @Lydia Park at 2026-03-19T13:58:02Z. Impact scope: onprem/private control plane.

Lydia Park: Confirming — change was to improve perf. We missed a test for KMS binding cases. Plan: add exception table where cluster-level admin roles (namespaced exception list: `onprem-admin`, `privctl-admin`) win over tenant allowlists for KMS and KMS-like resources. Also add an integration test that simulates `kms:keys.*` access with mixed bindings.

Alex Gomez: For triage: can we reproduce in staging quickly? If yes, we should patch policy engine to check for `resource==kms` and role==admin shortcut before short-circuiting. Example pseudocode: 
```
if resource in kms_resources and role in admin_roles:
  return ALLOW if admin_binding_found
else:
  continue default_eval
```

Samira: Repro steps I used (staging cluster):
1) apply same bindings
2) run `make kms-rotate` job as svc-edge SA
3) observe `permission denied` in controller logs

I can repro and will run the staging test after Jon lands the precedence patch.

Jon Patel: I'll implement the precedence exception. ETA: ~2h to get a CI-green PR for policy engine, then a canary deploy to internal staging. If all good, roll to customer clusters. I'll also add a metric `rbac.kms_rotation_denied_total{patch_rev}` so we can monitor during rollout.

Mira Chen: For immediate mitigation: can we manually bind the onprem-admin role with cluster-admin-level KMS grants for this tenant? That would be a stopgap while patch goes out. Also we should rotate the affected KMS keys after fix to be safe. @Samira can you coordinate with the customer? :white_check_mark: 

Samira: Yup, I'll coordinate and schedule manual bind + key rotation windows. I'll also collect the KMS audit events and share in this thread.

Lydia Park: Follow-ups (I'll track):
- Add integration test for KMS access paths (owner: eng-ml)
- Update RBAC runbook with precedence caveats (owner: eng-security docs)
- Add telemetry `rbac.eval_path` to audit events so we can see which rule short-circuited (owner: eng-platform)

Alex Gomez: Quick security note: watch for service-account impersonation edge-cases — if a tenant SA can impersonate an admin SA we still have escalation risk. Samira, check impersonation logs for svc-edge.

Samira: Good catch, will check impersonation. I already saw no immediate impersonation evidence but will validate.

Jon Patel: Assigning to myself: will open PR titled `policy-engine: kms admin precedence exception` and link here. Will include tests + metric.

Mira Chen: Thanks team. I won't mark this incident high yet, but setting as P1 if we see KMS rotation failures > 5% on canary. I'll update the customer and keep this thread current. :v:
